title: Gian's Perfect Innovations
disclaimer: These pages describe published US patent applications that were abandoned and never granted. They are concept revivals of those disclosures, not patents owned here, and not a freedom-to-operate opinion.

ideas.name: AuraClip Personal Air Monitor
ideas.cardPitch: Clip-on personal CO + PM2.5 monitor with BLE exposure maps.
ideas.pitch: A clip-on personal air monitor that shows live CO and PM2.5 on-device and pushes exposure maps to your phone. Built for commute, wildfire season, and indoor workshops.
ideas.upgrade: The abandoned core (US20150212057A1) already solved MCU-driven CO heater cycles plus pulsed PM sensing in a wearable shell with tool-free sensor swap. AuraClip keeps that sensing control loop, then adds BLE, modern low-power MEMS sensors, a color AQI ring, and a phone app that builds personal exposure heatmaps and alerts when you enter a bad pocket of air.
ideas.target: City cyclists, parents in wildfire zones, HVAC techs, and anyone who wants personal AQI instead of a city-average number.
ideas.whyNow: Wildfire smoke and urban PM are mainstream news. MEMS PM and electrochemical CO are cheap. Phones make maps trivial. The original packaging looked like a lab brick; a clip-on form factor with app UX fixes that.
ideas.next: Bench prototype: ESP32-C3 + Plantower-class PM + electrochemical CO, heater duty cycle from the patent logic, BLE GATT to a Flutter app, 3D-printed clip enclosure.
claims: Wearable housing with dual-line display of CO and PM.
Form factor meant to be worn or carried like a phone.
Microcontroller runs the CO sensor heating cycle.
Auto-calibration of the CO metal-oxide sensor in clean air.
Sampling + interpolation on the CO response curve to ppm.
Sampling + calculation for PM density (ug/m3) and AQI mapping.
Communication interface to external computer / smartphone / tablet.
Polymer casing with side opening for gas sensor and top opening for PM; sensors held by polymer clamps for tool-free swap.
ideas.fto: Google Patents legal status: Abandoned - failure to respond to an office action. Individual inventor; no grant issued. US application rights appear free to practice for this published disclosure, subject to other patents in the field. Flag: freedom-to-operate still needs a sweep of later granted wearable AQI patents (e.g. modular / networked monitors). This is US-only application abandonment; check other jurisdictions if international filings exist (none found in the Google Patents family for this number).
ideas.status: Abandoned - FAILURE TO RESPOND TO AN OFFICE ACTION (recorded 2016-07-19 on Google Patents legal events)

ideas.name: HeatFold Waste-Heat Sticker
ideas.cardPitch: Peel-stick foldable paper TEG that harvests waste heat for BLE beacons.
ideas.pitch: A peel-and-stick, foldable paper thermoelectric sticker that turns phone, laptop, or kettle waste heat into microwatts for a BLE beacon or trickle charge. Fold geometry is the power dial
ideas.upgrade: The abandoned KAUST filing (US20170244019A1) showed Bi2Te3 / Sb2Te3 thermocouples on paper, with origami / accordion folds to raise power density and temperature gradient. HeatFold productizes that into a consumer sticker: adhesive cold side, printable thermocouple traces, QR setup, and a tiny energy-harvesting PMIC that wakes a BLE tag. Target use is battery-free temperature logging on hot pipes, laptops, and food warmers
ideas.target: IoT hardware startups, facilities teams (steam / HVAC), outdoor gear makers, and makers who want battery-free sensors
ideas.whyNow: Ambient IoT and battery-free tags are real. Flexible TEG research matured. Paper / polymer substrates cut cost vs rigid BiTe modules. Consumers understand stickers; they do not understand lab TEGs
ideas.next: Sputter or screen-print a 10-couple strip on polyester paper, accordion-fold to 4 layers, measure open-circuit voltage on a warm laptop chassis, wire to an LTC3108-class harvester + BLE beacon
claims: Paper substrate with thermocouples in series between two contact points.
Substrate can be standard paper or polyester paper.
Each thermocouple is a pair of inorganic materials (exemplified Bi2Te3 and Sb2Te3).
Materials chosen by figure of merit ZT.
Deposition via PVD magnetron sputtering; contact pads join legs.
Folding (origami, accordion, fan) sets power density and max temperature gradient.
Fold can be changed later to retune power / gradient.
ideas.fto: University US application abandoned for failure to respond to an office action. No US grant on this number. Flag: KAUST and related authors may hold related publications or non-US filings; check family and later flexible-TEG grants before commercial scale. Paper-substrate plus fold-to-tune remains a strong good-core, weak-packaging case.
ideas.patentTitle: Flexible and foldable paper-substrate thermoelectric generator (TEG)
ideas.inventor: Jhonathan Prieto Rojas; Muhammad Mustafa Hussain
ideas.assignee: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
ideas.status: Abandoned - FAILURE TO RESPOND TO AN OFFICE ACTION (recorded 2019-01-30)

ideas.name: DewBar Sanitized Air Water
ideas.cardPitch: Countertop air-to-water bar with multi-tank heat sanitize and scald lock.
ideas.pitch: A countertop air-to-water bar that harvests humidity, heat-sanitizes the water in stages, and locks the cold faucet during sanitize so you cannot scald yourself. Hot and cold drinking water without bottles.
ideas.upgrade: The abandoned core (US20160244951A1) already combined dehumidifier harvest, multi-tank heat kill steps (collection + cold + hot), ceramic filtration, and a safety lockout on the cold faucet during sanitize. DewBar keeps that safety-first water path, then modernizes packaging: quiet VFD compressor, UV at point of dispense, IoT filter-life and sanitize schedule, and a solar-assist option for off-grid cabins.
ideas.target: Homes in humid climates with weak tap water trust, small offices, Airbnbs, and disaster-prep households.
ideas.whyNow: Plastic water bottles are politically and brand-toxic. Point-of-use AWG is shipping again. The missing piece in many units is honest sanitization plus scald-safe UX - exactly what this abandoned design already solved.
ideas.next: Breadboard control: Arduino/ESP control of heaters, solenoid lockout, and temp hold at 70-85 C for a timed sanitize cycle on a 5 L cold tank mockup. Validate kill-step timing, then design a quiet enclosure.
claims: Dehumidifier harvests and condenses atmospheric vapor.
Collection tank receives condensate.
First heater kills bacteria in the collection tank.
Tube from collection to cold tank with in-line filter(s).
Second heater kills bacteria in the cold tank (periodic sanitize).
Tube from cold tank to hot tank enabling convective mixing.
Tubes to external faucet(s) for cold and hot dispense.
Also disclosed: solenoid lockout so cold faucet cannot dispense during high-temp sanitize; control board + temperature sensors; user display to schedule sanitize cycles.
ideas.fto: Individual US application abandoned for failure to respond. No grant on this number. Flag: atmospheric water generator space is crowded with other patents (harvest hardware, membranes, etc.). The relatively distinctive piece here is multi-tank heat sanitization plus faucet lockout UX. FTO sweep required before productization; treat as inspiration plus a free published recipe, not a blank check.
ideas.patentTitle: Devices and methods for collecting, sanitizing, and dispensing condensed forms of atmospheric water
ideas.status: Abandoned - FAILURE TO RESPOND TO AN OFFICE ACTION (recorded 2018-04-18)

ideas.name: CoolClamp Clip-On Body Cooler
ideas.cardPitch: Clamp-anywhere upper-body cooler with PCM pack and face-aim arm.
ideas.pitch: A light upper-body cooler that clamps to a collar, strap, or bag and blows air across a phase-change pack. Built for hot flashes, outdoor sports, and crowded venues where you cannot carry a bulky vest.
ideas.upgrade: The abandoned core (US20150374046A1) is a clamp-mountable upper-body cooler with ice-pack compartment, fan, vents, speed control, and an elbow-like adjustable arm that lifts cool air toward the face. CoolClamp keeps clamps + pack + directional arm, then upgrades ice to reusable PCM packs, swaps the motor for a quiet USB-C fan, adds soft textile sleeves for skin comfort, and splits SKUs for menopause relief vs sports day-use.
ideas.target: People with menopause hot flashes, stadium / festival goers, outdoor workers, and e-bike riders in heat.
ideas.whyNow: Personal cooling wearables are a growing category, but most are heavy vests or neck fans with no thermal mass. PCM packs plus clamp-anywhere mounting is a clearer product story than the original DIY-feeling ice unit.
ideas.next: Sew or 3D-print a U-form shell with two spring clamps, a PCM pouch slot, and a 5V USB-C blower aimed at vent holes. Test face-directed arm geometry and wear time with one PCM pack.
claims: Upper-body cooler mountable to clothing via support structure with pack compartment, battery power, and blower.
Ice pack as cooling source; frozen damp sponge listed as alternate.
Blower pushes air through pack compartment and out vents.
Adjustable control switches for on/off and speed.
Clamps on both ends to attach to clothes.
Adjustable arm moves up/down/side like an elbow to aim air at the face.
Can wear around neck/shoulders or drape over one shoulder; arm and pack can sit on opposite ends.
Can run as a plain fan without ice.
ideas.fto: Individual filing abandoned for failure to respond. Core idea is simple and packaging-weak, which is exactly why it is a good upgrade candidate. Flag: personal cooling devices are common; uniqueness is clamp-anywhere + elbow aiming arm + pack compartment. Design around that, and run a quick FTO on neck fans and cooling scarves.
ideas.status: Abandoned - FAILURE TO RESPOND TO AN OFFICE ACTION (recorded 2017-08-30)
